text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Municipalities face added costs: Items that province left off balance sheet likely to be questioned at meeting today.
- Windsor Wal-Mart wins right to union: Firm intimidated staff, board rules.
- Alberta election set for March 11: Klein seeks endorsement of deficit fight; opposition argues cuts were too deep.
- Russia reserves first use of nuclear arms: Army's deterioration makes deterrence vital to defence policy, official says.
- CSIS knew RCMP worker had terrorist links: Mounties not told that man now on trial in infiltration case had been a high-ranking Tamil Tiger.
- Teachers makes power play: Pension board wants Cambridge to buy -- or sell -- stakes in 5 malls worth C$350-million.
- Investor ire looms over MacBlo loss: Quarterly red ink reaches C$72-million.
- Lunch bucket crowd gets rich in Kapuskasing: Tembec offer assures Spruce Falls' shareholders of windfall.
- Retail wars claim another victim: Greenberg bankruptcy kills 1,400 jobs.
- Gulf tightens grip on Clyde: Clyde stays defiant, but Gulf now has 28 percent of the British oil company and looks on the verge of emerging the victor in the takeover fight.
